name: Hyperkalemic Periodic Paralysis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Electrophysiological Diagnostic Criteria for Hyperkalemic Periodic Paralysis

criteria.description: Recurrent episodes of muscle weakness or paralysis lasting minutes to hours
Episodes associated with elevated serum potassium levels (hyperkalemia)
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the SCN4A gene
Electromyographic evidence of myotonia or abnormal muscle membrane excitability
Positive family history of similar episodic paralysis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent episodes of muscle weakness with documented hyperkalemia during attacks, supported by genetic testing or family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by laboratory and genetic findings; electromyography can aid in confirmation.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically affects proximal muscles and may involve respiratory muscles in severe cases
Serum potassium elevated during episodes but normalizes between attacks

common.notes: Mild muscle stiffness may precede or follow weakness episodes
Often reported during or between attacks

common.symptomName: Weakness triggered by rest after exercise

occasional.notes: Respiratory muscle involvement causing breathing difficulty
Rare but possible due to hyperkalemia
Mild muscle enlargement may be present

rare.notes: Occurs in longstanding disease with repeated attacks
Severe hyperkalemia may cause conduction defects
Rare complication during severe paralysis episodes

laboratory: Normal creatine kinase or mildly elevated
imaging: Usually normal; muscle MRI may show mild fatty infiltration in chronic cases
genetic: Pathogenic variants in SCN4A gene encoding the skeletal muscle sodium channel
other: Electromyography showing myotonia or abnormal muscle membrane excitability
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Episodes associated with low serum potassium
Different triggering factors such as carbohydrate-rich meals
Distinct genetic mutations (CACNA1S or SCN4A variants)
Predominant muscle stiffness worsened by cold and exercise
Less prominent or absent episodic paralysis
SCN4A mutations but different clinical presentation

references: Statland JM, Fontaine B, Hanna MG. Hyperkalemic periodic paralysis. GeneReviews. 2020.
Cannon SC. Channelopathies of skeletal muscle excitability. Compr Physiol. 2015.
Orphanet: Hyperkalemic periodic paralysis. Orphanet Journal of Rare Diseases. 2021.
